blocks.h: What happens after a fault report

items.d: Ticket by email; [a service engineer or dispatcher] calls within your severity's reply time and confirms the severity with you.
In the mode you allow, or from the readings and files you sent.
With the likely parts, calibrated reference instruments and training records for your induction.
Like-for-like repair and checks. Anything not like for like goes to your change control before water is used.
Within [service report turnaround, working days]: work done, as-found and as-left values, parts with lot numbers.

blocks.intro: Choose "Parts and consumables" in the form, or email [parts email address]. Orders go to [the parts desk or stores team], not the fault queue.

items.d: Call [service phone number]. Stocked parts ship from [spares stock location] [order cut-off and delivery commitment].
Quote the tag number from your turnover package, the serial or make and model, and the quantity.

items.t: Like for like, with the certificates
items.d: Each part ships with the certificates the qualified part had. Not like for like? We say so before you order.
Send make, model, original part number and a photo. [Confirm: parts supplied for other makes.]
Membranes, electrodeionization (EDI) modules and instruments from named manufacturers where the design allows, so you are not tied to one source.

items.q: Our system is from another builder. Can you service it?
items.a: Yes, no Aquemi serial number is needed. For a fault, choose "Fault now" and give the make and model. For a first planned visit, choose "First service, other make": we start with a condition survey and a records review. We service [makes and equipment types serviced]. Upgrades and assessments go to the proposal form.

items.q: Who decides whether water already used is affected?
items.a: Your quality unit. We give it the facts: when the readings left specification, which systems and points of use were affected, what we found and what we did, in the signed service report. We do not release water or close deviations.

items.q: We have no service plan. Will you come?
items.a: Yes, as a call-out with the next available technician, at [call-out rate and hourly rate, CAD]. Response times by severity and plan are on the service plans page.

items.q: Our IT allows no remote access to GMP equipment.
items.a: Choose "No remote connection". We diagnose from the readings and files you send and by phone with your operators. On-site response times are the same in every mode.

items.q: Can you work to our SOPs, forms and induction?
items.a: Yes. Name your standard operating procedures (SOPs) and forms in "Site access requirements" and "Whose forms do we work to?". We send training records with the visit plan and complete your work orders, logbooks or calibration forms as well as, or instead of, ours.

items.q: Is our site inside your service area?
items.a: Response times apply inside [service coverage area]. Outside it, we give a travel response time in the first reply, and plan holders have it written into the plan schedule. Service bases are on the locations page.

cta.h: Planning ahead, not fixing a fault?
cta.body: A service plan fixes response times, visits, calibrations and spares in writing, at a fixed annual price.
